title: Mūmiyāʾ — The Substance Before the Corpse
subtitle: How a mineral medicine became a mummy

claims.text: Foundational mūmiyāʾ was a valued mineral pitch/asphalt rather than originally a preserved corpse.
Fracture treatment was a defining medieval Arabic and Byzantine indication.
Corpse-associated mūmiyāʾ existed within Arabic medicine before its expansion in Latin Europe.
Some, but not all, later Egyptian mummies contained petroleum bitumen.
The single-mistranslation explanation is insufficient; analogy, translation, substitution, scarcity and commerce form a longer process.
The exact geological identity of prized Persian mūmiyāʾ remains uncertain.
